title: vbumper configuration
description: Schema for the vbumper project configuration file (e.g. `.vbump.yaml`).

version.description: Schema version marker. Must be 3 for this format.

version_tag_prefix.description: String prepended to the version when forming a Git tag name (e.g. "v" + "1.2.3" -> "v1.2.3", available to flow commands as the {VERSION_TAG} placeholder). Never applied to version strings written into files.

default_flow.description: Key of the flow to run when no --flow option is given on the command line, matching one of this file's own `flows` entries. Omit to have no default flow (equivalent to always requiring --flow or defaulting to no flow at all). Overridable per invocation with --flow=NAME or suppressed with --no-flow.

flows.description: Named Git release workflows. A flow is a sequence of pre-write-back commands, the version-file write-back itself, and a sequence of post-write-back commands. No flow receives any special treatment from vbumper: every option, precondition, and config value applies identically regardless of which flow (if any) is selected. Each entry is either a full definition, or a `recall` of a flow defined in `~/.vbumpconfig.yaml` with its own `variables` merged on top -- see `flowDefinition`.

discoverers.description: Version-file discoverers/recognizers to run. Every discoverer, built-in types included, is opt-in -- nothing runs unless listed here (e.g. `{type: pyproject-toml}` activates that built-in with no other keys needed). Each entry is a plugin config, discriminated by `type` (the plugin's registered identifier); remaining keys are plugin-specific and validated by that plugin, not by this schema.

exclude.description: Paths to keep out of version-file discovery, in addition to the built-in default exclude patterns (VCS dirs, language/build caches, IDE folders, editor swap files, etc.). Patterns use gitignore syntax (matched via `pathspec`'s gitignore matcher, e.g. `**/testing/`, `node_modules/`, `*.generated.py`, or `!keep/this` to negate a built-in default back open), evaluated against paths relative to the discovery root (--dir). A single pattern may be given as a bare string instead of a one-element list.

excludePatterns.description: One gitignore-style pattern, or a list of them.

flowKey.description: Identifier for a flow: lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens, starting with a letter.

flowDefinition.description: Either a full flow definition, or a `recall` of a flow defined in `~/.vbumpconfig.yaml` with only `variables` alongside it.

recall.description: Key of a flow defined under `~/.vbumpconfig.yaml`'s `flows:`. Adopts that definition wholesale (name, require_on_branch, pre_commands, stage_command, post_commands); this entry may only additionally set `variables`, merged key-by-key onto the recalled definition's own. Referring to a name not defined there is a configuration error.

name.description: Human-readable display name for this flow (used in help/list output). Purely cosmetic; the flow key is what --flow=NAME matches against.

require_on_branch.description: Git branch that must be checked out for this flow to run (e.g. "develop", or a {NAME} placeholder such as "{DEVELOP_BRANCH}" resolved against this flow's own variables). Omit to allow the flow to run from any branch.

pre_commands.description: Commands run, in order, before version files are written back. If any command fails, the flow aborts immediately and no write-back or post_commands run.

stage_command.description: Optional command, run once per file vbumper actually wrote back this run (in order), with {CHANGED_FILE} substituted to that file's path. Runs after write-back and before post_commands. Omit to stage nothing automatically -- vbumper never stages/adds anything on its own unless a flow opts in here, and this only ever touches the exact files vbumper itself wrote, never a blanket 'add everything dirty'.

post_commands.description: Commands run, in order, after version files are written back (and after stage_command, if set). If any command fails, the flow aborts immediately and no further post_commands run.

flowVariables.description: Arbitrary flow-specific data, each entry available to this flow's commands as a {NAME} placeholder (e.g. {"RELEASE_BRANCH": "main"} makes {RELEASE_BRANCH} available). Purely data substituted into commands -- vbumper never acts on the values directly. Keys may not be VERSION, VERSION_TAG, or CHANGED_FILE, which are always reserved for vbumper's own substitutions.

command.description: A single command, run through the operating system's own command shell after placeholder substitution (/bin/sh on Unix-like systems, cmd.exe on Windows). May contain the placeholders {VERSION} (the bumped version string, e.g. "1.2.3-rc.1"), {VERSION_TAG} (version_tag_prefix + VERSION, e.g. "v1.2.3-rc.1"), and one {NAME} placeholder per entry in this flow's own `variables:`. Substitution is verbatim -- no value is quoted or escaped on the command's behalf.

stageCommand.description: A single command, run once per changed file through the operating system's own command shell after placeholder substitution (/bin/sh on Unix-like systems, cmd.exe on Windows). Accepts everything `command` does, plus {CHANGED_FILE} (that invocation's file path) -- meaningless, and left unsubstituted, anywhere else. Substitution is verbatim -- no value is quoted or escaped on the command's behalf.

discovererConfig.description: Provisional shape: a plugin-discriminated config object. `type` selects the discoverer plugin; all other keys are that plugin's own parameters (e.g. a regexp-based discoverer takes `name`, `filename_pattern`, `content_pattern`). This section will be tightened once the plugin config schema registry (goal #1 / #4) is finalized.

type.description: Registered identifier of the discoverer plugin this config is for (e.g. "file-regexp").

nonEmptyPathspecPatterns.description: One gitignore-style pattern, or a non-empty list of them. Unlike `excludePatterns`, this can never be empty: a `file-regexp` discoverer's `include:` has no "match every file" default and must always narrow to at least one pattern.
